Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair

mechanism noun

the working parts of a machine

also mechanisms, machinery, the works, how it works

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.97: cum māchinātiōne quādam movērī aliquid vidēmus (Lewis & Short)

māchinātiō, māchinātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a mechanism, a contrivance

An artificial contrivance that makes a thing move; in Caesar also a machine or siege engine, and figuratively a trick, a machination (Lewis & Short), so the setting must make the mechanism clear.

Other words

  • māchina, māchinae f. — a machine, a device

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    The whole machine rather than its working parts (see machine); also a scheme or a trick (Lewis & Short).

  • agendī ratiō, agendī ratiōnis f. — the way something works, a mechanism (of a process)

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. mechanism (Trappen, 1843)

    For the figurative sense, the way a process works: “the mechanism of the disease”. Built on ratiō with a gerund (see process).

Examples

  • cum māchinātiōne quādam movērī aliquid vidēmus, ut sphaeram

    when we see something moved by some mechanism, like a celestial globeCic. N.D. 2.97 (Lewis & Short)

See also machine, engine, technology, process.

SourcesLewis & Short: machinatio · Lewis & Short: machina

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. mechanism.
